topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes students to the final lecture and outlines the overarching learning objectives regarding cancer therapy approaches and mechanisms.

topics.label: Conventional Modalities: Surgery, Radiotherapy, and Cytotoxic Chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine standard therapeutic approaches, discussing how physical resection, radiation, and non-specific cytotoxic drugs operate along with their clinical benefits and systemic toxicities.

topics.label: Targeting Intrinsic Cellular Vulnerabilities and DNA Repair Defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how therapy can exploit intrinsic cancer vulnerabilities, including hormone dependence, cell cycle checkpoint abnormalities, and defective DNA repair pathways.

topics.label: Oncogene Targeting with Kinase Inhibitors and Mechanisms of Resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on inhibiting hyperactivated oncogenic kinases and exploring the biological mechanisms and clinical management of acquired drug resistance.

topics.label: Monoclonal Antibodies and Antibody-Drug Conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover antibody-based therapies designed to target specific tumor surface markers either directly or by delivering cytotoxic payloads.

topics.label: Cancer Immunotherapies and T-Cell Engagement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the role of the immune system in cancer control and detail therapeutic approaches that re-engage or engineer T cells to eliminate tumor cells.

topics.label: Overarching Challenges, Historical Progress, and Future Directions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the systemic challenges in cancer treatment, historical improvements in patient survival, emerging prevention strategies, and ethical dilemmas surrounding therapy choices.
